thread:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — RDMA packet reassembly errors + container crashes detected on multiple serving nodes in rack-7. SEV2. auto-created incident: INC-3754321.

Maya (oncall): ack — I'm on it, fetching logs + impact.

Elena (SRE): I'm joining. can someone paste the failing node ids?

Jordan (eng-runtime): nodes: node-7a, node-7b, node-7c. pattern: sudden retransmit/reassembly errors, followed by CUDA OOMs and processes killed (serve binary).

Jordan (eng-runtime): logs (snippet):
```
May 03 14:02:33 node-7a kernel: mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: cq 1234 poll err -5
May 03 14:02:33 node-7a kernel: ib_retransmit: packet reassembly failed: frags=0x12 proto=0x81
May 03 14:02:34 node-7a serve[1234]: RuntimeError: CUDA failed to allocate 512MB
May 03 14:02:34 node-7a kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 1234 (serve) total-vm:643512kB
```

Maya (oncall): current alert rate? dashboards?

devops-bot: alert stream: 83 errors/min for model-x generate route, 12% 5xx rate increase across eu-west-3.

Priya (support): customers affected: a handful of high-volume tenants in eu-west. support already flagged 3 active incidents. sending initial customer advisory now.

Luis (netops): initial hunch: PMTU/jumbo-frame fragmentation or switch buffer congestion causing RDMA reassembly to fail. need to confirm if any recent MTU changes or switch flaps.

Elena (SRE): can we reproduce ib link check? @Luis can you run quick probes on node-7a?

Luis (netops): running ibv_rc_pingpong and ethtool/ibstat now.

devops-bot: command outputs attached to incident INC-3754321.

Luis (netops): ibv_rc_pingpong shows intermittent packet loss, RTT spikes and "transport retry exceeded" on qpn 0x12f. ethtool shows large rx errors on mlx5p2.

Jordan (eng-runtime): runtime workaround suggestion: flip to TCP fallback for the serving pool (REDWOOD_NET_TRANSPORT=tcp) for model-x to avoid RDMA path until netops confirms stability. CPU cost up but will stop OOM crash cascade. thoughts?

Elena (SRE): agreed — schedule a config toggle on the affected pool. we should also disable cross-node KV cache to reduce inter-node RDMA chatter.

Maya (oncall): I'll patch the serving group config to set transport=tcp and disable kvcache for the canary subset (10% traffic) first. if stable for 5m, roll to 100%.

Jordan (eng-runtime): doing canary now.

devops-bot: applying config patch to pool 'serve-eu-3-modelx' (canary=10%).

Maya (oncall): canary switched to TCP. monitoring metrics...

(devops-bot reaction): :white_check_mark: config apply success

10m later — Maya (oncall): canary looks good, error rate down to baseline for canary hosts. no crashes observed.

Elena (SRE): start rolling the rest of the pool with 30s staggered restarts to avoid stamping the cluster. ensure node drains before restart.

Jordan (eng-runtime): rolling now. also added env REDWOOD_DISABLE_GDR=1 on the rollout to force slower but safer CUDA path for these hosts.

Luis (netops): meanwhile I'm running a targeted switch health check. found a partial reconfiguration on TOR-7 with a firmware push 2 hours ago — buffers momentarily mis-sized for jumbo frames; vendor confirmed a bug that can cause fragmented IB packets to be dropped under load. not yet fixed by them.

Elena (SRE): good find. can we avoid vendor fix window by keeping TCP for the pool and draining cross-rack flows? Also add iptables rule to rate-limit large UDP/IB control frames?

Luis (netops): we can't easily block IB control in prod without vendor involvement. short-term plan: keep TCP fallback, move heavy KVcache traffic to nodes in rack-3 (which are healthy), and coordinate vendor patch for torque switch ASAP.

Priya (support): customer impact update for status page: "Partial service degradation in eu-west affecting generation latency and errors for some customers. Mitigation in progress; more details to follow." Shall I post now?

Elena (SRE): yes post now, note that mitigation may increase CPU and latency for affected workloads due to TCP fallback.

Maya (oncall): rolling restart finished. all affected nodes are now on TCP fallback and kvcache disabled. crash rate dropped to baseline, 5xx rate returned to normal.

Jordan (eng-runtime): runtime logs after mitigation: no new CUDA OOM kills. memory pressure is higher but within headroom.

Elena (SRE): action items: (1) keep pool on TCP fallback until vendor patch applied and we validate IB stability; (2) schedule a maintenance window to test MTU/firmware rollback; (3) run extended soak tests on rack-7 for 2 hours; (4) follow-up postmortem.

Luis (netops): vendor ETA for firmware fix: 8 hours. they provided a temporary recommended config to avoid the drop but it requires NOS change — needs maintenance window.

Priya (support): update posted to customers. collecting impacted customers for credit assessment.

Maya (oncall): handing off monitoring to night oncall @Elena. I will remain available for 30m for questions.

Elena (SRE): taking handoff — monitoring dashboards, alerts silenced for the pool while we keep TCP fallback. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. assigning follow-ups -> postmortem, vendor ticket, maintenance scheduling.

inc-bot: Incident INC-3754321 status updated: mitigated -> handoff to SRE night.

Maya (oncall): thanks team. good job triaging fast. :thumbsup:

Jordan (eng-runtime): notes for postmortem: correlate IB reassembly errors with firmware push timeline, review auto-scaling behavior under TCP fallback to avoid cost shock, add preflight checks for MTU on deploys.

Elena (SRE): I'll create the postmortem doc and link action items. closing thread when postmortem exists.
